rationale: Both refactors make the same core improvements, each with a clear log. They validate up front, replace the hand-rolled sort with sort.Slice on a copy, drop the goroutine fan-out and extract small helpers. B adds nice touches: named column-width constants, sentinel errors, time.Parse for date validation and rune-aware padding. However, B's formatAmount has a real grouping bug. The loop writes everything except the last three digits and then a separator, so 1234567 cents' integer part comes out as "1234,567" instead of "1,234,567". B's truncate comment also wrongly says it elides the middle. A's groupThousands is correct for any magnitude. Its fmt.Sprintf with width verbs, which pad by rune count, keeps the layout compact and readable. Its only blemish is checking the currency twice. Because A gets amount formatting correct beyond the tested range, it is the better refactor.
